title: Implementation notes — Durable ingestion journal
subtitle: phase 3 of 5 complete · 2026-09-22 20:38 CDT
intro: Each item is a decision, deviation, or tradeoff made during implementation. Acknowledge if fine. Discuss to write what should change. Revert to flag for undo.

groups.label: Phase 1 — Freeze the contract and add schema 10
Phase 2 — Implement journal storage and writer recovery
Phase 3 — Route every capture surface through the journal
Phase 4 — Add owner operations and adversarial tests
Phase 5 — Document, verify, and cut over the Mac Mini

items.title: Queued outcome exposure stays with Phase 3

body.Spec said: Define CaptureOutcome now, then route capture surfaces through queued outcomes in Phase 3.
body.What I did: Added and exported the closed CaptureOutcome union, but kept the current CaptureTask protocol and public-job sink typed as returning CaptureReceipt until queued outcomes are implemented and routed.
body.Why: No Phase 1 implementation can return a queued outcome yet. Exposing the union through the live task protocol early produced 86 MyPy failures across consumers that correctly assume today's terminal-only behavior.
body.Risk: Phase 3 must widen the task protocol and update every consumer in the same verified change.

body.What I did: Injected a fixed drain clock into fixed-timestamp tests and used a fresh enqueue time for the real subprocess lease test.
body.Why: The baseline fixtures crossed their 24-hour retry-age boundary during verification on September 22. They quarantined before transport and failed independently of the journal changes.
body.Risk: None to production behavior; this only removes wall-clock dependence from tests.

body.What I did: Completed the journal and custody contracts, schema-10 catalog and exclusive migration, Portable Brain v5 export gate, runtime compatibility bump, and regression coverage.
body.Why: The Phase 1 exit gate is satisfied and the repository's full verification command passes.
body.Followup: Phase 2 implements journal storage, bounded drain, recovery, terminalization, and compaction.

items.title: Public capture routing stays with Phase 3

body.Spec said: Phase 2 builds the journal and writer recovery; Phase 3 routes CaptureTasks and adapters through it.
body.What I did: Kept CaptureTasks.accept, CaptureTasks.submit, source revision capture, and Markdown import on their existing terminal-only writer path. Phase 2 exercises enqueue directly and drains it through engine recovery.
body.Why: Routing the public surfaces here would pull Phase 3 forward, widen the live return protocol early, and mix adapter cutover with the journal correctness boundary.
body.Risk: The journal is durable and recoverable but ordinary capture calls do not use it until Phase 3.

items.title: Canonical overlap preserves active custody replay

body.What I did: When a crash leaves both an active journal item and its same-digest captures row, replay resolves through the active journal item. It returns the original custody receipt until the writer records the terminal receipt and compacts the payload.
body.Why: That overlap is an expected crash state after capture reservation or canonical completion, not ambiguous storage. Different digests or a tombstone overlap still fail closed.
body.Risk: A replay during this short window may receive queued even if canonical stages have finished; the next bounded writer drain terminalizes it without creating another capture.

items.title: Quarantine and byte bounds stop automatic overrun

body.What I did: Excluded quarantined entries from automatic drain, enforced the aggregate batch-byte ceiling from the first item, and rejected limit configurations where one permitted item cannot fit in one permitted batch.
body.Why: Quarantine requires owner action, and a byte bound must remain exact without creating an undrainable first item.
body.Risk: Deployments must configure max_journal_batch_bytes at least as large as max_journal_item_bytes.

body.What I did: Implemented durable enqueue and exact receipt replay, bounded FIFO drain, capture materialization under the existing writer fence, terminalization, guarded compaction, retry, quarantine, discard, metadata-only status, and capture-first startup recovery.
body.Why: Crash-boundary, overlap, quarantine, batch-bound, schema, and contention coverage pass. The repository's full verification command is green: 3,336 Python tests with 5 expected skips, 291 Obsidian tests, 259 desktop tests, and 26 Rust tests.
body.Followup: Phase 3 routes every capture entrypoint and upstream custody adapter through the journal while preserving explicit EffectiveAuthority.

body.What I did: Routed CLI, MCP, collector, connector, source revision, and Markdown capture through durable enqueue before bounded writer drain. A schema-10 engine can open read-only while another process owns the writer fence, accept the journal item, and return queued custody.
body.Why: The Mac Mini owns the payload after journal commit. Writer contention should delay canonical materialization, not send the payload back to the source for another retry.
body.Risk: Callers must handle the closed CaptureOutcome union. Terminal-only compatibility properties now raise if queued custody reaches code that has not handled it. They add no fields to the signed receipt wire format.

items.title: Replay and upstream verification preserve receipt bindings

body.What I did: Kept exact replay bound to the original requested privacy tier, while preserving the final narrowed tier from canonical capture. Collector and connector consumers verify digest, Brain identity, journal epoch, delivery identity, privacy narrowing, and protection before acknowledging custody or completion.
body.Why: Compaction and replay must not rewrite what the source requested, and an upstream adapter must not delete its copy on a receipt for another payload or weaker privacy boundary.
body.Risk: A changed digest or widened tier is rejected even when other signed receipt fields are valid. This is intentional fail-closed behavior.

body.What I did: Kept source compare-and-swap checks under the writer fence and blocked Portable Brain export while a source-backed journal item is quarantined.
body.Why: The source revision remains pending until canonical capture completes. Exporting while that revision is unresolved could present an incomplete Brain as portable state.
body.Followup: Phase 4 adds explicit owner inspection, retry, and discard operations for this state.

body.What I did: Cut every capture surface over to journal custody, preserved explicit EffectiveAuthority through adapters, updated production consumers for queued outcomes, and covered contention, replay, outbox terminalization, receipt tampering, source fencing, and recovery.
body.Why: The Phase 3 exit gate is satisfied. Full verification is green: 3,341 Python tests with 5 expected skips, 291 Obsidian tests, 259 desktop tests, 1 desktop Python test, and 26 Rust tests. Ruff, MyPy, TypeScript, builds, and Rust formatting also pass.
body.Followup: Phase 4 adds explicit owner journal operations and the remaining adversarial and observability coverage.
